title: The Sharp Worst-Case Asymptotic Rate of the Barzilai--Borwein Method in $\mathbb R^d$ and Hilbert Spaces
summary: We establish sharp asymptotic rates for the two Barzilai--Borwein (BB) rules on uniformly positive quadratics and local nonlinear problems. In finite dimensions, for either fixed rule and an arbitrary positive first step, the gradient root factor is bounded by $(b_0-a_0)/(b_0+a_0)$, where $[a_0,b_0]$ is the initially active spectral interval. Hence the worst trajectory factor is $c_H=(κ(H)-1)/(κ(H)+1)$. When $H$ has at least two distinct eigenvalues, matched initialization and a balanced endpoint trajectory attain this value.
